releases.title: Quiet background orchestration
releases.summary: Pauses decorative Intelligence motion when StatsKey is hidden, unfocused, or locked, keeping Fleet and live sync available without wasting local GPU.
highlights: Hidden, unfocused, and locked Intelligence windows stop decorative repainting while Fleet and live sync continue.
Animations resume immediately when StatsKey returns to focus.
The six-task ceiling, shared collaboration, output redaction, decline guards, and event-driven indexing remain unchanged.

releases.title: Unattended orchestration hardening
releases.summary: Keeps Mac mini work visible and collaborative while preventing stalled local indexing and ensuring native task authorization remains usable.
highlights: Native Fleet job review now stays onscreen while retaining digest-bound exact authorization.
Shared Mac mini tasks report collaborative workspace phases consistently in the live Intelligence timeline.
Workspace file changes are coalesced so remote viewing no longer triggers minute-by-minute full rescans.
Background indexing now uses a 30-minute safety refresh and remains single-flight under heavy sync activity.
Delegated tool allowlists, six-task scheduling, redaction, retry guards, and merge behavior remain covered by 204 tests.

releases.title: Direct Mac mini Intelligence
releases.summary: Run an ordinary Intelligence tab on the Mac mini, follow sanitized progress and file changes locally, and open its encrypted screen in a lightweight fullscreen controller.
highlights: Choose This Mac, Mac mini · collaborate live, or Mac mini · isolated copy from the Intelligence header.
Remote-owned tabs send the actual prompt to the mini and restore their live task card after a tab or app reload.
Delegation enforces a six-task turn cap, signed tool allowlists, decline-safe retries, and stricter remote-output redaction.
The fullscreen screen controller keeps frame memory bounded and falls back safely if its renderer stalls.
Mac input readiness reports missing Accessibility permission instead of silently claiming control.

releases.title: Intelligence run convergence
releases.summary: Intelligence now recognizes pending nudges, bounds answer-only evidence loops, and finishes with a tool-free handoff instead of extending the action log.
highlights: A nudge now resumes the unfinished implementation with its original completion contract.
Answer-only evidence work switches to final synthesis after six tool rounds or 24 completed actions.
Intermediate direct-provider decisions have a five-minute absolute limit while final handoffs retain their longer allowance.
Live activity reports completed actions without presenting a growing log length as a fixed finish line.

releases.title: Reliable remote screen startup
releases.summary: Fleet remote sessions now start the capture command, restore live viewer state, and fail cleanly instead of showing a permanent black panel.
highlights: Narrowly authorizes video-only capture for StatsKey's registered hidden screen renderer.
Waits for a real capture track before marking a remote session active.
Restores relay and stream-header state even when connection events arrive before the viewer mounts.
Ends failed or timed-out capture commands instead of leaving zombie sessions.

releases.title: Live Intelligence delegation
releases.summary: Watch and control Mac mini work directly inside Intelligence while local work continues.
highlights: Persistent live task cards show state, current activity, sanitized remote output, and observed files.
Refresh and cancel controls work directly from Intelligence without another chat message.
Adaptive polling supports six concurrent tasks without abandoning audited agent supervision.
Approval-window failures no longer masquerade as user declines.

releases.title: Visible, verifiable Intelligence approvals
releases.summary: Delegate from Intelligence with foregrounded, compact native approvals that keep controls visible, bind the complete job by digest, and distinguish cancellation from client failure.
highlights: Delegate to another enrolled machine directly from an Intelligence chat while local work continues.
Compact exact-job approval sheets keep Approve and Cancel visible above the macOS Dock.
A SHA-256 digest binds every normalized job field, including any previewed prompt tail.
Window, renderer, and validation failures remain retryable and no longer appear as user declines.

releases.title: Intelligence delegation that stays visible
releases.summary: Delegate directly from Intelligence with native approvals that foreground StatsKey, distinguish cancellation from client failures, and remain retryable when approval UI is unavailable.
highlights: Delegate to another enrolled machine directly from an Intelligence chat while local work continues in the same run.
Fleet approval sheets now foreground StatsKey and serialize concurrent prompts.
Window, renderer, and validation failures no longer masquerade as a user decline.
Cancelled approvals stay fail-closed without repeated prompts in the same turn.

releases.title: Live sync and task delegation across your machines
releases.summary: Mirror a folder live between your enrolled machines from the Cockpit, hand a plain-English task to another machine and watch it run, and get more reliable Mac fleet workers.
highlights: Start a live sync from a Cockpit device card to mirror a folder between two machines in real time.
Delegate a plain-English task to another machine from the Cockpit and follow its progress live.
Fleet workers on macOS now report available memory correctly.
Remote screen sessions add a Screen Share button on the Cockpit device card.

releases.title: Organize workspace files in place
releases.summary: The Workspace now has a Files panel on the right: browse, create, rename, delete, and drag-and-drop files and folders without leaving the editor.
highlights: Organize workspace files from the right-side Files panel.
Create, rename, delete, and drag-and-drop files and folders in place.

releases.title: Cockpit in the sidebar
releases.summary: The Cockpit now sits in the desktop sidebar for one-click access to your machines, alongside the tab bar.
highlights: Cockpit is always reachable from the desktop sidebar.

releases.title: Cockpit: your machines in one view
releases.summary: The new Cockpit tab shows your enrolled machines as cards with one-click remote sessions, task runs, and file browsing, plus a one-time optional introduction for new desktop users.
highlights: The Cockpit tab shows your machines as cards with remote session, task, and file actions.
New desktop users get a one-time optional Cockpit introduction; chat stays the default landing.
Create a project folder with just a name from the Cockpit or the workspace start page.

releases.title: Fleet remote sessions
releases.summary: StatsKey can now open a remote desktop session to your enrolled Windows workers from the Fleet tab, end-to-end encrypted through your own relay.
highlights: Remote desktop sessions to enrolled Windows workers from the Fleet tab.
Sessions are approved per device and encrypted end to end through your own relay — no third-party service.
Ubuntu worker service attestation now refreshes continuously instead of expiring in place.

releases.title: Helpers that stay in step
releases.summary: Investigators follow the active model and provider route by default, with one quiet advanced control for choosing any available StatsKey or My key route.
highlights: Investigators inherit the chat's model, provider, billing route, and service tier by default.
The advanced Helper model control can choose any runnable StatsKey or configured My key route.
Ask and Plan can use read-only helpers while action review stays limited to action modes.
Platform-aware preparation keeps Mac and Windows versions, links, and signing disclosures aligned.
Private source provenance and launch health checks make each published build reproducible and verifiable.

releases.title: Windows and Ubuntu desktop previews
releases.summary: The Windows preview keeps investigators on the active model route by default, and the Ubuntu 26.04 LTS x64 preview adds an explicit DEB package with secure storage checks and fail-closed Fleet control.
highlights: Windows investigators inherit the main model and provider route by default.
Native Windows checks bind the public installer to install, restart, workspace, terminal, browser, and update-readiness proof.
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS x64 has an explicit DEB package and native release-proof contract.
Credentials are refused when Electron falls back to unprotected basic-text storage.
Ubuntu can control Fleet while unattended worker execution remains disabled pending a protected service.

releases.title: Helpers that follow your lead
releases.summary: Investigators now follow your chosen model unless you quietly customize them, final answers stay active while providers are healthy, and releases use one guarded path from build to launch.
highlights: Investigators now inherit the main model and provider route by default.
An advanced Helper model control can assign a different configured model without cluttering the everyday interface.
Final responses no longer stop at the former one-minute cutoff while the provider remains healthy.
A deterministic Mac release command now builds, publishes, installs, launches, and verifies the same artifact.

releases.title: Public boundary correction
releases.summary: A focused Mac correction removes a residual private-machine command path from the public package and strengthens the checks that guard future releases.
highlights: The public Mac package no longer contains the dormant Remote Access execution path that remained in 0.21.5.
Compiled assets are now checked for Remote Access, MacRemote, Oil Data, remote-command, and private-machine markers before publishing.
The clearer mode chooser and reviewable customization workflow from 0.21.5 are unchanged.

releases.title: A clearer, more approachable workspace
releases.summary: The mode chooser is now fully visible and easier to understand, StatsKey can open its own source for reviewable customization, and public packages remove Founder-only interfaces.
highlights: The mode chooser stays inside the window, scrolls on compact screens, and has a clear Close control.
Automatic is clearly recommended, while Ask, Plan, Fix, and Execute explain their outcomes in plain language.
Model, context, and action controls remain under Advanced settings, while change permission appears only for an explicit Fix or Execute choice.
Settings can open a reviewable StatsKey source workspace so you can describe the changes you want to Intelligence.
Public packages remove the internal Founder console, privileged Founder bridge, Founder runtime, and legacy Founder switches.
Release verification rejects known Founder routes, commands, and artifacts before publishing.

releases.title: Consent controls that stay reachable
releases.summary: The Intelligence disclosure now fits every supported desktop window without trapping the workspace or hiding its controls.
highlights: Disclosure details scroll independently when the window is compact.
Not now and Enable remain visible while you review the disclosure.
Not now exits the full-page disclosure or closes the workspace panel instead of redirecting back into it.
An accepted choice remains saved and unlocks Intelligence across tabs.

releases.title: Clean recovery when a provider pauses
releases.summary: StatsKey now preserves completed workspace work and ends the active pass cleanly when a model provider reaches its response deadline.
highlights: A provider deadline no longer restarts the same failed autonomous pass.
Completed files, checkpoints, and verification remain saved for a clean continuation.
Managed Kimi now uses bounded requests, provider timeouts, and server-authoritative credit reservations.
Stripe billing and third-party connector authorization now use the hardened live backend.

releases.title: Work that stays with its workspace
releases.summary: StatsKey now keeps active tasks bound to the workspace where they started, while bringing billing, provider access, and third-party tools into one clearer setup.
highlights: Active tasks continue against their original workspace when you switch tabs, folders, or projects.
Execute mode can run independent work concurrently while serializing only conflicting edits.
Connections & billing centralizes Stripe, Google, GitHub, model providers, and OAuth or MCP tools.
Model selection explains pricing, adds ChatGPT Fast and Kimi, and accepts any model returned by a connected provider.

releases.title: Windows, tested where it runs
releases.summary: The Windows preview now passes a native install, launch, restart, workspace, terminal, browser, and update-readiness gate before it can be published.
highlights: Workspace changes remain available after restarting the Windows app.
Commands, installed apps, and Android tools follow the Windows environment automatically.
The release process binds the public installer to native Windows test evidence.
Completion stays tied to saved results and successful verification.

releases.title: Proof you can inspect
releases.summary: StatsKey can now exercise mobile work directly and only calls implementation complete when the saved result and its verification agree.
highlights: Simulator Lab can discover, start, inspect, and interact with iOS Simulators and Android emulators.
Completed workspace changes include persisted-change and verification evidence you can review.
Files, search, browser tabs, and workspace navigation are easier to find and use.
Long-running work settles reliably in the background and keeps its final verification visible.

releases.title: Desktop preview
releases.summary: The first public StatsKey workspace preview.
highlights: Project workspaces, local tools, model choices, and update delivery.
A conversational work log with review preferences and resumable sessions.
